content: 1. Yasuda MA conducted a study comparing parasitemia levels of Trypanosoma cruzi in patients with chronic Chagas disease who were either HIV-positive or HIV-negative. The findings were published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2002, volume 186, issue 6, pages 872–875. 2. Perez-Ramirez L and colleagues analyzed the clinical manifestations and genetic diversity of Trypanosoma cruzi in HIV/Chagas co-infected patients in Brazil. This study was published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 1999, volume 61, issue 2, pages 198–206. 3. Brito CMM, Pires MQ, and Pacheco RS investigated the genetic characteristics of two Trypanosoma cruzi strains under experimental immunosuppression in the context of Chagas disease and HIV co-infection. Their findings appeared in Kinetoplastid Biology and Disease in 2003, volume 2, article 107. 4. Revera J, Hillis LD, and Levine BD reported on the reactivation of cardiac Chagas disease in patients with acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS). This case was documented in the American Journal of Cardiology in 2004, volume 94, issue 8, pages 1102–1103. 5. Valerga M and colleagues described a case of multifocal encephalitis in a patient with AIDS, published in Enfermedades Infecciosas y Microbiología Clínica in 2005, volume 23, pages 569–570. 6. Picco G highlighted the importance of considering Chagas disease and AIDS as a co-infection in clinical practice. This was published in Medicina Clínica (Barcelona) in 2005, volume 125, page 679. 7. Burgos JM and collaborators used molecular techniques to diagnose and type Trypanosoma cruzi populations in a patient with cerebral Chagas disease and AIDS. This study was published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2005, volume 73, issue 6, pages 1016–1018. 8. Cordova E and colleagues documented cases of Chagas disease reactivation with central nervous system involvement in HIV-infected patients in Argentina between 1992 and 2007. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2008, volume 12, issue 6, pages 587–592. 9. Rodriguez Guardado A and collaborators conducted a screening for Chagas disease in HIV-positive immigrants from endemic areas. This study was published in Epidemiology and Infection in 2011, volume 139, issue 4, pages 539–543. 10. Almeida EA and colleagues studied the prevalence, clinical presentation, and natural history of Chagas disease and HIV co-infection in patients without effective antiretroviral therapy. Their findings were published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2010, volume 104, issue 7, pages 447–452. 11. López O reported a clinical case of chagasic meningoencephalitis in an HIV/AIDS patient who survived for three years. This case was published in the Revista Chilena de Infectología in 2010, volume 27, issue 2, pages 160–164. 12. Warley E and colleagues described the development of neoplasms and AIDS-defining infections after initiating highly effective antiretroviral therapy. This study was published in Medicina (Buenos Aires) in 2010, volume 70, issue 1, pages 49–52. 13. Almeida EA and collaborators reported on the diagnostic challenges in distinguishing between reactivation of myocarditis and chronic chagasic cardiomyopathy in Chagas/AIDS co-infection. This study was published in the Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de Medicina Tropical in 2009, volume 42, issue 2, pages 199–202. 14. De Almeida EA and colleagues evaluated the efficacy of itraconazole or ketoconazole for treating Trypanosoma cruzi and HIV co-infection. Their findings were published in Annals of Tropical Medicine and Parasitology in 2009, volume 103, issue 6, pages 471–476. 15. Burgos JM and collaborators identified Trypanosoma cruzi I tropism for the central nervous system during Chagas reactivation in AIDS patients. This study was published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2008, volume 78, issue 2, pages 294–297. 16. Sica RE and colleagues described tumor-like chagasic encephalitis in AIDS patients, including an atypical presentation and outcomes in a small series of cases. This was published in Arquivos de Neuro-Psiquiatria in 2008, volume 66, issue 4, pages 881–884. 17. Verdú J and collaborators reported on Chagas disease reactivation with central nervous system involvement, providing evidence from peripheral blood smears. This study was published in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2009, volume 13, issue 6, pages e527–e528. 18. Bisio M and colleagues documented the successful treatment of chagasic encephalitis with benznidazole in a pregnant woman with AIDS. This case was published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2013, volume 19, issue 9, pages 1490–1492. 19. Solari A and collaborators reported on the successful treatment of Trypanosoma cruzi encephalitis in a patient with hemophilia and AIDS. This study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 1993, volume 16, issue 2, pages 255–259. 20. Rocha A and colleagues described a case of Trypanosoma cruzi meningoencephalitis and myocarditis in a patient with AIDS. This case was published in the Revista do Instituto de Medicina Tropical de São Paulo in 1993, volume 35, issue 2, pages 205–208. 21. Metze K and Maciel JA reviewed the relationship between AIDS and Chagas disease, published in Neurology in 1993, volume 43, issue 2, pages 447–478. 22. Oddó D and colleagues reported two cases of acute Chagas disease in AIDS patients. This study was published in Human Pathology in 1992, volume 23, issue 1, pages 41–44. 23. Gluckstein D and collaborators identified Chagas disease as a cause of cerebral mass lesions in AIDS patients. This case was published in the American Journal of Medicine in 1992, volume 92, issue 4, pages 429–432. 24. Rosemberg S and colleagues described fatal meningoencephalitis caused by Trypanosoma cruzi reactivation in an AIDS patient. This case was published in Neurology in 1992, volume 42, issue 3, pages 640–642. 25. Gallo P and collaborators reported on acute central nervous system infection by Trypanosoma cruzi in an AIDS patient. This study was published in Arquivos de Neuro-Psiquiatria in 1992, volume 50, issue 3, pages 375–377. 26. Ferreira MS and colleagues described a case of acute fatal Trypanosoma cruzi meningoencephalitis in an HIV-positive hemophiliac patient. This case was published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 1991, volume 45, issue 6, pages 723–727. 27. Torre Alba G and collaborators emphasized the value of brain biopsy in AIDS patients with cerebral mass lesions. This study was published in the Revista Médica de Chile in 1990, volume 118, issue 12, pages 1367–1371. 28. Livramento JA and colleagues analyzed cerebrospinal fluid abnormalities in 170 AIDS cases. This study was published in Arquivos de Neuro-Psiquiatria in 1989, volume 47, issue 3, pages 326–331.
